# flux7

> Governance for AI agents: a sidecar between agents and their tools that decides what an agent may do. flux7-mesh (L0, policy in under a millisecond), flux7-memory (L1, past human approvals of reads), flux7-supervisor (L1+, rules then a decision model, a few hundred milliseconds), a human in flux7-console or the mesh CLI (L2). Every decision is traced in a hash-chained log. mesh7, mem7, sup7 and the console are Apache 2.0.

Start with "How it works", then "Getting Started". Configuration lives in one YAML file for the mesh (`config.yaml` plus policy files) and one for the supervisor (`sup7.yaml`).

## Start

- [What flux7 does](https://docs.flux7.art/evaluate/): for evaluators, what is governed, what you get, what it does not do, how it is deployed
- [Features](https://docs.flux7.art/evaluate/features/): every capability per component with its maturity (stable, early, planned)
- [How it works](https://docs.flux7.art/how-it-works/): the four layers, what each one asks, and the path of one tool call
- [Getting Started](https://docs.flux7.art/getting-started/): install flux7-mesh, first policy in front of Claude Code, approve a call, read the trail; then add the other products
- [Govern Claude Code](https://docs.flux7.art/guides/claude-code/): MCP tools through the proxy, built-in tools through the hook, observe then enforce
- [Hold risky calls for a human](https://docs.flux7.art/guides/risky-calls/): conditions on arguments, the approval queue, grants, precedents and the supervisor

## flux7-mesh (mesh7)

- [Overview](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/): what the sidecar does, MCP over stdio and HTTP, REST
- [Configuration](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/configuration/): every key of config.yaml (upstreams, auth, approval, supervisor, memory, traces)
- [Writing Policies](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/writing-policies/): rules per agent and per tool, conditions on arguments, allow / deny / human_approval
- [Tool Classification](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/tool-classification/): read / write / generic families, catalogue pinning
- [Approval Flow](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/approval-flow/): the queue, grants, the wait window, settings editable at runtime
- [Memory Integration](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/mem7-auto-approve/): when past human approvals approve a read, and why writes always ask
- [Supervisor Protocol](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/supervisor-protocol/): the HTTP contract a supervisor uses to resolve approvals
- [JWT Authentication](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/jwt-auth/): agent and human identity from OIDC tokens (JWKS, issuer, audience, claims)
- [Control Plane Auth](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/control-plane-auth/): how data-plane and control-plane endpoints are authorized differently
- [Behind Keycloak and Kong](https://docs.flux7.art/guides/keycloak-kong/): mesh7 behind an API gateway with delegated identity
- [Deployment Modes](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/deployment-modes/): local sidecar, shared instance, with or without supervisor
- [Observability](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/otel/): OpenTelemetry export and trace context over MCP
- [Trace Integrity](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/trace-integrity/): the hash-chained trace log and how to verify it
- [Agent Security](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/security/): why agents with tools need governance, and what the mesh enforces
- [CLI Tools](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/cli-tools/): govern CLI tools (terraform, kubectl, docker, gh, cloud CLIs) through the mesh
- [Python SDK](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/python-sdk/): `pip install flux7-mesh`, govern tool calls from any Python code (Claude API, Agent SDK, LangChain)
- [Reference](https://docs.flux7.art/mesh7/reference/): commands, flags, HTTP API and repository layout

## flux7-memory (mem7)

- [Overview](https://docs.flux7.art/mem7/): decisions kept as queryable facts
- [Configuration](https://docs.flux7.art/mem7/configuration/): environment variables and server settings
- [API Reference](https://docs.flux7.art/mem7/api-reference/): MCP tools and HTTP endpoints
- [Python SDK](https://docs.flux7.art/mem7/python-sdk/): `from mem7 import Mem7` (PyPI package: flux7-memory)

## flux7-supervisor (sup7)

- [Overview](https://docs.flux7.art/sup7/): the L1 supervisor, rules then a chain of decision providers, admin API, POST /evaluate
- [Configuration](https://docs.flux7.art/sup7/configuration/): every key of sup7.yaml
- [Jev and question sets](https://docs.flux7.art/sup7/jev/): narrow typed questions, the decision taken in code from probabilities
- [Measuring](https://docs.flux7.art/sup7/measuring/): the bench of labelled cases and how thresholds are chosen
- [Claude Code Callback](https://docs.flux7.art/sup7/claude-code-callback/): Claude Code as a provider (marked not functional)

## flux7-console

- [Overview](https://docs.flux7.art/console/): the operator UI (approvals, traces, policies, supervisor)
- [System Design](https://docs.flux7.art/console/system-design/): the design of the whole stack
